negative_findings.description: All direct fetches to bqk-kos.org (HTML register page and the dated PDF list of licensed financial institutions) returned HTTP 403 during this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 Forbidden on https://bqk-kos.org/mbikeqyrja-financiare/institucionet-financiare-te-licencuara-2/?lang=en and on the 22.04.2026 PDF. Search engines index the same URLs, so the site is bot-defended rather than dead. The exact list of licensed IP/IPE entities could NOT be read in this run and must be treated as unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The canonical actor list for this entire cell is behind that defence; without a headless-browser collector the pipeline cannot enumerate licensed EMIs/PIs authoritatively and will over-rely on media reports.

negative_findings.description: No Kosovo fintech/EMI/PI in this cell was found to operate a conventional investor-relations page, annual report, or structured press-release archive.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for funding/press releases returned coverage in third-party media (Telegrafi, Koha advertorials, SeeNews, The Recursive) and LinkedIn company pages, never a company newsroom or IR section. FIKS, the sector cluster, also has no news section.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Workstream A1 topics (annual reports, investor relations, earnings) are structurally absent for non-bank payment actors in Kosovo; collection design must substitute media, advertorial and app-store channels or the cell will look empty.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language (sr) searching produced almost no Kosovo-specific non-bank payment sources.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries in Cyrillic and Latin Serbian on doznake / platne institucije / transfer novca / Kosovska Mitrovica returned Serbia-domestic material (NBS payment-fee registers, Pošta Srbije PostCash, NLB Komercijalna) and the note that NLB Komercijalna closed its Kosovo branches in Feb 2024. No Kosovo-licensed Serbian-language payment institution or MTO source was identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Serb-majority north is a real remittance and cash corridor, but its payment infrastructure appears not to be documented in publicly indexed sr sources tied to Kosovo — a genuine blind spot rather than a search failure, and one that also implies parallel/unlicensed channels are invisible to this method.

negative_findings.description: Speculative Kosovo payment-gateway brand names (PCPS, Kosova Pay, Pay24, Klix) returned no evidence of existence in this market.
negative_findings.result_summary: The sq gateway query returned only regulatory PDFs, the eKosova state platform, and merchant blogs naming Paysera and Revolut as the practical acceptance options. None of the guessed brands were corroborated; they are recorded as not-found, not as sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that domestic online-acquiring brands are thin or absent and that foreign EMIs (Paysera, Revolut) fill the gap — a structural fact about the cell, and a warning against seeding actor maps from guessed names.

negative_findings.description: "Kosovo e-Wallet" is not a payment product.
negative_findings.result_summary: The App Store app named Kosovo e-Wallet is a digital identity wallet published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs, not an e-money or payment wallet. Keyword-based collection on 'wallet' will produce false positives for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents mis-classification of a government identity credential as an EMI product in the actor map; also flags 'portofol digjital' as a noisy term.

coverage_gaps.description: The definitive list of BQK-licensed payment institutions (IP), e-money institutions (IPE) and registered currency-exchange offices (ZKV) was not readable this run due to the 403, so the cell's actor map rests on media-derived names (Paysera Kosova, OneFor, Swinto/Velanis, Numarics, MPAY/KUIK, UFP).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a headless-browser or proxied collector for bqk-kos.org, fetch the latest 'Lista e institucioneve financiare' PDF, parse the IP/IPE/ZKV sections, and use it as the authoritative seed list for all subsequent passes.

coverage_gaps.description: Own-domain URLs for Paysera Kosova, OneFor, Swinto and Numarics were not confirmed in this run; only LinkedIn company pages and media coverage were verified as discovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up pass resolving each actor's official domain (and any /newsroom, /shtypi, /lajme path) via ARBK legal-entity lookup and app-store publisher fields, then register those domains as direct sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-Western-Union MTOs active in Kosovo (MoneyGram, Ria, Small World, Wise, Remitly and bank-hosted remittance products) were not individually mapped; only the Western Union agent UFP was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query each MTO brand name in sq alongside 'agjent', 'pika', 'tarifat' and cross-check against the BQK licence list and World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide corridors (DE→XK, CH→XK).

coverage_gaps.description: No sr-language Kosovo payment/remittance source was located; the Serb-majority north's payment channels remain undocumented in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Try outlet-scoped sr searching (KoSSev, Kontakt Plus, Radio Gorazdevac) on 'plaćanja', 'doznake', 'menjačnica', 'kartice' and check whether Serbian-system institutions still operate any Kosovo-facing payment points.

coverage_gaps.description: No financial-statement-level disclosure source exists for this cell: EMIs/PIs in Kosovo publish no annual reports and their filings, if any, were not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check whether ARBK or the tax administration publishes filed financial statements for LLCs, and whether BQK's periodic financial-stability/payment-system reports break out non-bank PSP volumes; if neither, mark A1 'annual reports/earnings' as structurally unavailable for this cell.

brief: Kosovo's non-bank payment layer is regulator-documented but corporately silent: BQK holds the only authoritative actor list (licence PDFs for IP/IPE/ZKV, plus the e-money and PI authorisation regulations and the pending Law on Payment Services), yet its site returned 403 to every automated fetch this run and must be collected with a browser-grade agent. The commercial actors themselves — Paysera Kosova (reported first EMI licence), OneFor, Swinto/Velanis, Numarics, MPAY/KUIK and Western Union's principal agent Unioni Financiar Prishtinë — publish essentially nothing resembling annual reports or investor relations; their disclosures surface instead as Albanian-language press items and paid advertorials (Telegrafi, KOHA reklama-marketing), regional wires (SeeNews, The Recursive), LinkedIn company posts, published tariff pages, and app-store release histories. Demand-side sizing for the remittance segment, which no operator discloses, comes from GAP Institute, GERMIN and World Bank/UNDP diaspora reporting. The main structural gaps are the unread licence register, unresolved official company domains, an unmapped set of non-WU money-transfer operators, and a real Serbian-language blind spot over the north.
